title: Evidence Studio: investigate, test and reconsider
idea: Build a compelling middle-school fictional science investigation, replacing the earlier long worksheet with a visual evidence studio. The learner helps a fictional school garden team decide what the available evidence supports. Start with invented plant observations A (water 1 story unit/day; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves) and B (water 2; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves). A learner chooses a claim and the pair of evidence cards supporting it. Reveal C (water 2; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves) as a counterexample without requiring a changed answer. All cards are an invented 14-day story, not measurements, plant-care advice or real outcomes. Starting height, plant type and soil are unrecorded; final height is not growth and leaves do not validate health. Turn comparison into an interactive visual activity with clearly labeled height graphics and visible differences in recorded conditions. Provide a small test-planning bench where learners choose which conditions to hold constant and inspect two clearly fictional prepared comparisons. Use fixed invented examples rather than a purported scientific plant-growth calculator. Describe which recorded conditions differ and what remains unknown; do not automatically judge the learner. End with a correctable before/after claim and selected evidence, including retain, narrow, revise or withhold. Offer a second optional comparison with fewer claim suggestions as supported practice in a changed situation, not proof of transfer. Facilitation, paper activity and dissent remain first-class routes. The product should invite investigation, not present nine empty text fields.
domain: Middle-school science inquiry and reasoning from fictional evidence
people: Students with varied reading and language access, science teachers, classroom support staff and caregivers; none are participants in this demonstration.
constraints: Keep all original domain constraints: no real student records, automated grades, rankings or inferred disability. Shared device; keyboard operation, clear focus, readable responsive layout and a complete teacher-facilitated paper alternative. Provide a strong opening mission, at most two open-text entries on the main learner path, evidence-card pair selection, meaningful claim/evidence comparison, staged reveal and a test-planning interaction whose choices visibly affect the displayed fictional comparison. Keep uncertainty and dissent. Prevent silent replacement of learner wording; provide cancel, correction and within-group recovery; clear all application-owned data and recovery on confirmed handoff. Explain ordinary browser/privacy limits without a wall of warnings. No network, storage, telemetry or external assets. Candidate HTML may be up to 26000 characters. Use inline SVG or CSS for legible visuals, with text equivalents. Review metadata belongs in a compact review/help panel; invented-data labels remain on evidence. Product quality must be inspectable in a complete Design and Build brief: need, learner/system capabilities, interaction journey, source-linked requirements, why each choice matters, tradeoffs, observable acceptance checks, technical evidence status and remaining field questions. All teacher, student and caregiver review, human pilot and learning/transfer/flourishing evidence remain pending. The previous school-science run is the parent iteration, not new evidence or an approved baseline. A design may still be rejected; do not treat aesthetics or completion as demonstrated learning.
